# Micro-Benchmark: Latency and Determinism in Autonomous Edge Systems

A Comparative Study of Local Inference Engines

Author: Devendra Thapa

Affiliation: Department of Software Engineering, Pokhara University, Nepal

Date: September 2026

Correspondence: d.thapa@pu.edu.np
content.Abstract: Edge intelligence requires predictable low-latency query execution without reliance on remote cloud infrastructure. This micro-benchmark paper quantifies memory footprint and execution variance across lightweight quantized transformer models running locally on standard edge hardware. Our benchmarks demonstrate an average latency of 28.5 milliseconds for 128-token contextual queries.
content.Keywords: edge intelligence; quantization; deterministic latency; local inference; micro-benchmark
content.1. Introduction: Deploying language models on edge devices demands deterministic bounds on latency and memory footprint. When network connectivity is intermittent, local inference guarantees continuity of operations.
content.2. Literature and Related Work: Recent advances in model quantization have substantially reduced parameter sizes while preserving perplexity scores.
content.3. Methodology / Approach: We deployed a local runtime engine and conducted 500 consecutive query probes measuring cold-start and warm inference latency.
content.4. Results and Discussion: Warm query latency averaged 28.5 ms with a standard deviation of 1.2 ms. Peak RAM usage stabilized at 2.1 GB during active decoding.
content.5. Conclusion: Local edge inference provides deterministic, high-throughput capability suitable for mission-critical offline document querying.
